A.explanation: Balance means the wire p.d. exactly opposes the test cell e.m.f., so no net p.d. drives current through the galvanometer branch.

B.explanation: The driver loop with the $6\text{ V}$ supply, resistor $R$ and wire is unchanged, so the driver current through $R$ is the same in both tests.

C.explanation: Cell e.m.f. is proportional to balance length, and $44\text{ cm} < 70\text{ cm}$, so cell X has the smaller e.m.f., not larger.

D.explanation: A balance is found on the wire, so each e.m.f. is balanced by only part of the driver p.d. and must be less than the $6\text{ V}$ driver.

walkthrough: The top loop with the $6\text{ V}$ driver, resistor $R$ and potentiometer wire is the same in both diagrams, so driver current $I$ and wire potential gradient are the same for the X and Y tests.
At the balance point the galvanometer reads zero because the p.d. across the used length of wire exactly balances the test cell e.m.f., with no current in the lower cell-galvanometer branch.
For uniform wire, p.d. is proportional to length, so $E = k l$ with the same constant $k$ in both tests.
Since $l_X = 44\text{ cm}$ and $l_Y = 70\text{ cm}$, then $E_X / E_Y = 44/70 < 1$, so $E_Y$ is larger than $E_X$.
Both balances occur within the wire length, so each $E$ is only a fraction of the total driver p.d. and must be less than $6\text{ V}$.
